note: The cleanest core match in the batch and arguably in the corpus — it meets all five criteria without argument. Successful: professional office role with clients of his own, maintains homes in both Atlanta and New York, genetics graduate. Income: zero price resistance and an unprompted benchmark against existing spend — 'that number is fine by me if it works... I pay my personal trainer far more than that... I'm not afraid of paying someone for what they're worth.' Neglected_health in its precise sense: not a crisis at all, but mobility and flexibility are the area he has deprioritised for four years while training everything else. Good_to_great is close to verbatim from the stated ICP — 'I'm pretty happy with my physique now, but it could also be a lot better.' Not_deconditioned: four to five gym sessions a week, four years of consistent strength training, and the opposite of gym-averse. The finding worth carrying to the rollup is that a perfect-ICP, pre-sold, price-accepting buyer did not close, and the reason had nothing to do with fit — the rep declined to send a payment link when asked. Read alongside the Chris Wiley call, where an off-script $1,200 tier was invented for a core-ICP buyer who had already accepted $6,000, the pattern is that ICP is not the constraint on this rep's revenue; the closing mechanics are.
